requirements.requirement: At least 512 MB of compressed in-memory swap configured on node1
requirements.summary: zram-init installed and configured with type0=swap, size0=512, algo0=zstd. swapon --show and zramctl confirm /dev/zram0 is a 512M zstd-compressed swap device, both before and after reboot.

requirements.requirement: zram swap active at boot without manual intervention
requirements.summary: zram-init was added to the default OpenRC runlevel (rc-update add zram-init default, confirmed by rc-update show default). A full reboot was performed; the post-restart boot_id differs from the pre-restart baseline, and swapon --show/zramctl/rc-service status immediately after reboot show the 512M zstd zram0 swap active and the service started, with no manual start command issued after reconnection.

requirements.requirement: zram swap preferred over any disk-backed swap
requirements.summary: /etc/fstab shows only the root filesystem entry, no disk-backed swap exists on node1. The zram swap was configured with the default near-maximum priority (16383, flag0 left empty per zram-init's documented default), which would rank it above any lower-priority disk swap; this priority is confirmed both pre- and post-reboot.

overall_summary: The task is fully satisfied: node1 has 512MB of zstd-compressed zram swap configured, enrolled in the default OpenRC runlevel, and demonstrated active immediately after a full reboot (with a verified change in boot_id proving the restart actually occurred) with no manual intervention. No disk-backed swap exists, and the zram device carries the near-maximum default priority, ensuring it would be preferred over any disk swap. The mandatory node-restart evidence protocol was completed with a clear pre-restart baseline, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and full post-restart recovery of the swap and service state.
limitations: Preference over disk-backed swap is demonstrated by configuration (high priority) and absence of any competing disk swap rather than an observed side-by-side priority race, since no disk swap exists on this node to directly compare against.
Two small log files (/tmp/apk_update.log, /tmp/reboot.log) were left on node1 after the task; minor and non-destructive but not cleaned up.

operational_hygiene.summary: All state-changing commands (apk add zram-init, sed edit of /etc/conf.d/zram-init, rc-update add + rc-service start, and the reboot) map directly to satisfying the swap requirement or the mandatory restart-evidence protocol. One failed attempt (`rc-update -a zram-init default`, invalid syntax) caused no state change and was immediately corrected with the working `rc-update add` form. The only residue is two small log files the executor redirected output into (/tmp/apk_update.log, /tmp/reboot.log), visible in the after-executor temporary-files diff; these are low-risk, non-destructive leftovers that were never cleaned up. No failed/conflicting services, no new listening sockets (socket diff is only PID/DHCP churn from the reboot itself), and package-health output is unchanged from baseline.
